questions.q: Why did Nag decide to wait in the bathroom until morning?
choices: The big man would come to bathe without his stick
The bathroom was the only cool place left in the house
Nagaina had told him to guard the sluice for her
He was too tired to crawl back out to the garden
questions.evidence: when he comes in to bathe in the morning he will not have a stick

questions.q: Where did Rikki-tikki decide he had to bite Nag?
choices: On the thick neck just below the hood
Near the tail, where the snake could not reach
On the head, above the hood
In the middle of the back, to break it

questions.q: Why did Rikki-tikki keep his jaws locked even when he was sure he would be banged to death?
choices: He hoped the big man would hear and come to help
For his family's honor, he wanted to be found holding on
He was too dizzy and frightened to let go of the snake
He wanted to prove to Darzee that he was not a coward
questions.evidence: for the honor of his family, he preferred to be found with his teeth locked

questions.q: What was the "thunderclap" that went off just behind Rikki-tikki?
choices: The heavy water jar falling and smashing on the floor
The big man firing both barrels of a shotgun into Nag
The tin bath being knocked over by Nag's thrashing tail
A storm breaking over the bungalow in the middle of the night
questions.evidence: fired both barrels of a shotgun into Nag just behind the hood

questions.q: Why was Rikki-tikki angry when he found Darzee singing a song of triumph?
choices: Darzee was taking all the credit for killing Nag
The singing had woken Teddy before breakfast
Nagaina was still alive, so it was no time to sing
Darzee had promised to keep the news a secret for now
questions.evidence: Is this the time to sing?

questions.q: Where had Nagaina hidden her eggs?
choices: Under the rubbish heap behind the stables, in the shade
In the melon bed, at the end nearest the wall
In the old rat-hole under the thorn-bush
Among the roots of the big orange tree
questions.evidence: In the melon bed, on the end nearest the wall

questions.q: "Darzee was a feather-brained little fellow." What does "feather-brained" mean?
choices: Silly and unable to think much ahead
Clever and quick to make plans
Shy and afraid of everyone
Very proud of his bright and beautiful feathers
questions.evidence: Darzee was a feather-brained little fellow

questions.q: Who actually pretended to have a broken wing to lead Nagaina away from the melon bed?
choices: Darzee himself
Chuchundra
Darzee's wife
The Coppersmith

questions.q: Why was Darzee's wife willing to help destroy the cobra eggs when Darzee was not?
choices: Nagaina had once tried to eat her own eggs
She knew cobra eggs would become young cobras
Rikki-tikki had promised to guard her nest forever
She wanted the melon bed for her own new nest
questions.evidence: she knew that cobra's eggs meant young cobras later on

questions.q: Why did Darzee's wife refuse to look at Nagaina when the snake told her to?
choices: A bird that looks into a snake's eyes is too frightened to move
She was busy watching for Rikki-tikki in the melon patch
She did not want Nagaina to see that she was not really hurt
She was ashamed of lying to the snake about the boy and the stone
questions.evidence: a bird who looks at a snake's eyes gets so frightened that she cannot move

questions.q: When Rikki-tikki found the eggs he said, "I was not a day too soon." What did he mean?
choices: Nagaina was about to move the eggs to a new hiding place
The baby cobras inside were almost ready to hatch
The ants were about to find and eat the eggs first
Teddy was planning to dig up the melon bed that day
questions.evidence: he could see the baby cobras curled up inside the skin

questions.q: When Rikki-tikki reached the veranda, where was Nagaina?
choices: Wrapped around the leg of the breakfast table
Coiled on the matting close to Teddy's bare leg
Lying across the veranda steps to block the door
Hanging from the roof above Teddy's mother
questions.evidence: within easy striking distance of Teddy's bare leg

questions.q: What happened the moment Nagaina spun around to look at her last egg?
choices: Teddy's father dragged Teddy across the table out of reach
Rikki-tikki bit Nagaina on the back of her hood
Teddy's mother fainted and fell from her chair
Darzee's wife flew down and flapped at Nagaina's head
questions.evidence: catch Teddy by the shoulder, and drag him across the little table

questions.q: How did Nagaina manage to get her egg back?
choices: She tricked Rikki-tikki by pretending to go away
She grabbed it while Rikki-tikki was drawing breath
She knocked Rikki-tikki off the veranda with her tail
Darzee rolled it toward her from the edge of the steps
questions.evidence: while Rikki-tikki was drawing breath, she caught it in her mouth

questions.q: How did Darzee's wife help Rikki-tikki catch Nagaina before she escaped?
choices: She flapped about Nagaina's head and slowed her down
She called the Coppersmith to block the path
She showed Rikki-tikki a shortcut through the long grass
She pecked the egg out of Nagaina's mouth
questions.evidence: the instant's delay brought Rikki-tikki up to her

questions.q: Darzee sings, "Valiant Rikki-tikki is dead!" What does "valiant" mean?
choices: Very small
Brave
Clever and sly
Quick-tempered

questions.q: What job does the Coppersmith bird do in the garden?
choices: He wakes the whole garden every morning at dawn
He is the town crier who tells everyone the news
He keeps watch for snakes from the top of the tallest tree
He mends the nests of birds after a storm
questions.evidence: he is the town crier to every Indian garden

questions.q: What is this part of the story mostly about?
choices: Rikki-tikki defeating both cobras to save Teddy's family
Darzee writing songs to honor the bravest animals
Teddy's family deciding to leave the dangerous bungalow
Nagaina teaching her young cobras how to hunt
questions.evidence: He saved our lives and Teddy's life
